title: White Oak: Ancient White Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Logan, Ohio's white oak is put at roughly six hundred years and still supplies the acorns for its own replacements. Three mapped across the US.
intro: White oak is eastern North America's slow, wide-crowned oak, tougher and longer-lived than red oak, and the three we map range from a fundraiser to a courtroom curiosity. The oldest, on the edge of Old Logan Cemetery in Ohio, is put at roughly six hundred years; the town sells its acorns as saplings to keep the line going. Boston's grows wild on the Arnold Arboretum's Peters Hill turf, uncatalogued until 2010 and cored in 2018 to roughly two centuries old, possibly the oldest tree in the whole collection. Athens, Georgia's is younger and stranger: an eighty-year-old planted in 1946 from the acorn of a white oak an 1890 newspaper story said legally owned itself, a claim courts have never accepted and the city has never stopped repeating.
